author: Seneca
quotes: While we are postponing, life speeds by.
Nothing, Lucilius, is ours, except time.

author: Seneca
quotes: We suffer more often in imagination than in reality.
So look forward to better things.

author: Seneca
quotes: And one day, mind you, is a stage on life’s journey.
Every morning he arises he receives a bonus.

author: Seneca
quotes: Learn how to feel joy.
The very soul must be happy and confident, lifted above every circumstance.

author: Seneca
quotes: We break up life into little bits, and fritter it away.
Such a life is not made happier for being longer.

author: Seneca
quotes: Infinitely swift is the flight of time.
How many steps for how short a climb!

author: Seneca
quotes: No one has any right to draw for himself upon the future.
The very thing that we grasp slips through our hands.

author: Seneca
quotes: The joy which entered from without will some day depart.
For the soul is more powerful than any sort of Fortune.

author: Marcus Aurelius
quotes: You do each act as though it were your last.
Brief is the life of each of us.

author: Marcus Aurelius
quotes: You should stand upright, not be held upright.
Choose the higher and hold fast to that.

author: Marcus Aurelius
quotes: While you have life, while you may, become good.
Do not wander without a purpose.

author: Marcus Aurelius
quotes: Where it is possible to live, there also it is possible to live well.
After a fall return again.

author: Marcus Aurelius
quotes: Make the best use of the present.
Love the men among whom your lot has fallen, but love them truly.

author: Marcus Aurelius
quotes: Let not the future trouble you.
Delve within; within is the fountain of good.

author: Marcus Aurelius
quotes: Accept without pride, relinquish without a struggle.
See that you bestow this present time upon yourself.

author: Marcus Aurelius
quotes: Be intent only on what is now being done.
When you have done good, what more, oh man, do you wish?

author: Epictetus
quotes: Of things some are in our power, and others are not.
Remember that in life you ought to behave as at a banquet.

author: Epictetus
quotes: Nothing great … is produced suddenly.
The matter of the art of living is each man’s life.

author: Epictetus
quotes: If you would make any thing a habit, do it.
Count the days on which you have not been angry.

author: Epictetus
quotes: First say to yourself Who you wish to be.
Do you wish to do good or to be praised?

author: Henry David Thoreau
work: Walden, Where I Lived, and What I Lived for
quotes: I went to the woods because I wished to live deliberately.
Our life is frittered away by detail.

author: Henry David Thoreau
quotes: Only that day dawns to which we are awake.
Rather than love, than money, than fame, give me truth.

author: Henry David Thoreau
quotes: I find it wholesome to be alone the greater part of the time.
I never found the companion that was so companionable as solitude.

author: Henry David Thoreau
quotes: The mass of men lead lives of quiet desperation.
As if you could kill time without injuring eternity.

author: Henry David Thoreau
quotes: In Wildness is the preservation of the World.
To enjoy a thing exclusively is commonly to exclude yourself from the true enjoyment of it.

author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
quotes: My life is for itself and not for a spectacle.
Trust thyself: every heart vibrates to that iron string.

author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
quotes: Nothing is secure but life, transition, the energizing spirit.
The only sin is limitation.

author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
quotes: For every thing you have missed, you have gained something else.
Every sweet hath its sour; every evil its good.

author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
quotes: The only way to have a friend is to be one.
A friend may well be reckoned the masterpiece of nature.

author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
quotes: To finish the moment, to find the journey’s end in every step of the road.
Life is a series of surprises.

author: Michel de Montaigne
work: Essays, Book 1, That to Study Philosophy Is to Learn to Die
translator: Charles Cotton, edited by W. C. Hazlitt
quotes: Where death waits for us is uncertain; let us look for him everywhere.
Young and old die upon the same terms.

author: Michel de Montaigne
translator: Charles Cotton, edited by W. C. Hazlitt
quotes: When I dance, I dance; when I sleep, I sleep.
The glorious masterpiece of man is to live to purpose.

author: Michel de Montaigne
work: Essays, Book 3, Of Managing the Will
translator: Charles Cotton, edited by W. C. Hazlitt
quotes: A man should lend himself to others, and only give himself to himself.
Custom is a second nature, and no less powerful.

author: Robert Louis Stevenson
quotes: There is no duty we so much underrate as the duty of being happy.
Extreme busyness … is a symptom of deficient vitality.

author: Robert Louis Stevenson
quotes: To travel hopefully is a better thing than to arrive.
The true success is to labour.

author: Robert Louis Stevenson
quotes: You must be open to all impressions and let your thoughts take colour from what you see.
Freedom is of the essence.
